issues.description: The problem statement gives conflicting requirements for the SealSaloon.stock attribute: one place (line ~70) describes it as a final instance field initialized in the constructor, while a later section (lines ~77-81) explicitly states the stock attribute must be static (shared across instances). The solution implements stock as a static final field. This contradiction in the problem text (instance-final vs static-final) will confuse students about whether to implement stock as an instance or static attribute and where to initialize it.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: decide whether stock is an instance-final field initialized in the constructor or a static-final shared field. Update the problem statement, UML and examples to say "private static final Stock stock" (and that it is shared and can be initialized at declaration) OR keep it instance-final and remove the instruction that stock must be static. Ensure the template and UML match the chosen design.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a method named checkOrderReady() (and instructs orderMeal() to call it), but the solution implements and calls a method named processOrders() instead of checkOrderReady(). This name/signature mismatch between the specified API and the solution implementation could confuse students when comparing behavior or tests that expect the named method.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the API names: update the problem statement to require processOrders() instead of checkOrderReady(), or rename processOrders() in the solution/template to checkOrderReady() (and keep its behavior). Alternatively, implement checkOrderReady() that delegates to processOrders() so both the specified name and the implemented logic exist.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a method named checkOrderReady() to process and serve pending orders, but the solution implements this functionality in a method named processOrders(). This introduces a naming mismatch for the same conceptual operation (checking and serving ready orders). Students reading the problem will look for checkOrderReady() to implement and tests or instructions may refer to that name, causing confusion when the solution uses a different identifier.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method processOrders() to checkOrderReady(), and ensure orderMeal() calls checkOrderReady(). Alternatively, add a public checkOrderReady() wrapper that delegates to processOrders(), so the method name in the implementation matches the problem statement and UML while preserving existing logic.
